name: key_sort_order
why: Python sorts keys by code point; Go sorts strings by UTF-8 byte. Those agree for valid UTF-8, and this case is what proves it rather than the argument that they do

name: empty_and_escaped_keys
why: keys go through the same string encoder as values; an encoder that escapes only values passes every value-only corpus

name: html_characters
why: encoding/json escapes < > & to \u003c \u003e \u0026 unless SetEscapeHTML(false); Python never escapes them

name: backspace_and_formfeed
why: Python emits the short forms \b and \f; encoding/json emits \u0008 and \u000c

name: line_and_paragraph_separators
why: encoding/json escapes U+2028/U+2029 as \u2028/\u2029; Python with ensure_ascii=False passes them through raw

name: non_ascii_passthrough
why: ensure_ascii=False means non-ASCII is raw UTF-8, not \uXXXX

name: non_bmp
why: the gateway sends json.dumps with ensure_ascii=True, so an emoji arrives on the wire as a surrogate PAIR and must canonicalise back to one raw 4-byte UTF-8 sequence

input.s:
quote" back\ slash/ tab	 nl
 cr

name: short_form_escapes
why: the escapes both encoders agree on -- included so a rewrite that gets the disagreements right cannot get these wrong unnoticed

name: control_characters
why: everything below 0x20 without a short form is \u00xx with LOWERCASE hex in Python; DEL (0x7f) is NOT escaped by either

name: numbers
why: 9007199254740993 is the integer float64 cannot hold: decoding into `any` renders it 9007199254740992. -0.0, 1e+21 and 1e-07 pin Python's repr formatting, which Go's strconv does not reproduce

name: nesting_and_empty_containers
why: an encoder that special-cases the empty object usually forgets the empty array, and vice versa

name: array_of_objects_keeps_order
why: arrays are ORDERED and must not be sorted; only object keys are

name: net_sweep_params
why: a realistic NetSweepParams (docs/modules/ipam/spec.md §5). `targets` is hashed as given, so its order must survive canonicalisation

name: health_policy_apply_params
why: a realistic HealthPolicyApplyParams (docs/modules/endpoint-health-alerting/spec.md). `threshold` and `value` are strings by design; a numeric threshold here would be a different signed byte string

name: job_payload_shape
why: the exact shape app/jobs/engine.py::_payload signs: seven keys, params nested, timestamps as rfc3339 strings

name: adversarial_mixture
why: everything at once, nested -- the case that catches an encoder correct at the top level and wrong one frame down
